### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Generic Springer Nature editorial policy (no Virtual-Reality-journal-specific AI page confirmed — the journal's own Ethics & Disclosures page sat behind an idp.springer.com login/cookie redirect that could not be fully resolved). Policy facts (paraphrased, not verbatim): LLMs cannot be listed as authors; substantive use of an LLM in preparing a manuscript must be disclosed in the Methods section (or equivalent); 'AI-assisted copy editing' of human-written text (grammar/style polishing) is explicitly exempt from disclosure; generative-AI-created images are not allowed in publications (narrow case-by-case exceptions); peer reviewers are explicitly asked not to upload manuscripts into generative AI tools. This is disclosure-gated rather than an outright ban, so scored 3/5 leniency; scored low signal_quality because it is publisher-wide, not confirmed journal-specific. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Multidisciplinary VR/AR/MR/XR research: (1) systems & enabling tech — displays, haptics, tracking/motion capture, 3D spatial audio, interaction techniques, real-time visualization; (2) applied domains — medical/surgical training & rehabilitation, industrial/manufacturing, education, design, entertainment, defense; (3) human factors — UX, psychology, motion sickness, accessibility, ethics/social/legal aspects of immersive tech. Confirmed by both the aims-and-scope page and the actual Vol. 28 Issue 3 (Sept 2024) table of contents (34 articles spanning CNN-based hand tracking, AR neurosurgical drain insertion, VR chronic-pain therapy, VR acrophobia exposure therapy, collaborative virtual environments, motion-sickness mitigation, VR education/training, product evaluation in VR, in-car VR usability).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** empirical/experimental user studies, systems design & evaluation papers, case studies / application projects, medical & clinical simulation studies, state-of-the-art review papers (general scope only; excluded from the now-closed 2025-26 Connected Realities collection)
